questions.question: Which of the following can help secure your sensitive data in Amazon S3? (Choose TWO)

options.text: Delete the encryption keys once your data is encrypted.

explanation.summary: Deleting encryption keys makes encrypted data permanently inaccessible and does not improve security.
explanation.why: Encryption keys are required to decrypt and access data. Deleting keys is a destructive action that results in permanent data loss rather than controlled protection. AWS security best practices focus on key management, rotation, and access control, not key deletion.

options.text: With AWS you do not need to worry about encryption.

explanation.summary: AWS does not automatically remove customer responsibility for data encryption.
explanation.why: Under the AWS Shared Responsibility Model, customers are responsible for protecting their data. AWS provides encryption capabilities, but customers must choose and configure them correctly.

explanation.summary: Enabling Amazon S3 encryption protects data at rest automatically.
keyPoints: Encrypts objects stored in S3 at rest
Integrates with AWS Key Management Service
Helps meet compliance and regulatory requirements
examples: Storing sensitive customer records in an S3 bucket with SSE-KMS enabled
Protecting backups stored in S3 using default bucket encryption
explanation.additionalInfo: Amazon S3 server-side encryption ensures that data is automatically encrypted when written to disk and decrypted when accessed by authorized users. This protects data against unauthorized physical access to storage media and supports compliance standards such as HIPAA, PCI DSS, and GDPR. Customers can enforce encryption using bucket policies to prevent unencrypted uploads.

options.text: Encrypt the data prior to uploading it.

explanation.summary: Client-side encryption protects data before it reaches Amazon S3.
keyPoints: Data is encrypted before transmission to AWS
Encryption keys are managed by the customer
Provides full control over cryptographic process
Protects data even from AWS access
Often used for highly sensitive data
examples: Encrypting files locally before uploading them to S3
Using envelope encryption for regulated workloads
explanation.additionalInfo: Client-side encryption ensures that AWS never sees unencrypted data. This approach is commonly used in highly regulated industries or when customers require complete ownership of encryption keys. It can be combined with server-side encryption for defense in depth.

options.text: Delete all IAM users that have access to S3.

explanation.summary: Removing IAM users does not directly secure stored data.
explanation.why: Security is achieved through least-privilege access and proper policy management, not by deleting users. IAM roles, policies, and permissions should be managed carefully instead of removing all access.

questions.question: Which AWS service helps developers compile and test their code?

explanation.summary: AWS CodeDeploy focuses on application deployment, not build or test activities.
explanation.why: CodeDeploy automates deployments to compute services but does not compile or test source code.

explanation.summary: AWS CodeCommit is a source control service.
explanation.why: CodeCommit stores and versions code but does not compile or execute tests.

explanation.summary: CloudEndure is used for migration and disaster recovery.
explanation.why: It replicates systems for migration or recovery and is unrelated to application builds or testing.

explanation.summary: AWS CodeBuild compiles source code, runs tests, and produces build artifacts.
examples: Running unit tests during a CI pipeline
Compiling Java or Node.js applications automatically
explanation.additionalInfo: AWS CodeBuild eliminates the need to provision and manage build servers. It executes build commands defined in a buildspec file and integrates tightly with AWS CodePipeline and CodeCommit. CodeBuild charges only for build time, making it cost effective for continuous integration workflows.

questions.question: Which of the following will affect how much you are charged for storing objects in S3? (Choose TWO)

options.text: Using default encryption for any number of S3 buckets.

explanation.summary: Default encryption does not increase S3 storage cost.
explanation.why: Amazon S3 does not charge extra for server-side encryption using SSE-S3. Encryption is included as part of the service.

options.text: The number of EBS volumes attached to your instances.

explanation.summary: EBS volume usage is unrelated to S3 storage pricing.
explanation.why: Amazon EBS and Amazon S3 are separate services with independent pricing models.

options.text: The storage class used for the objects stored.

explanation.summary: Different S3 storage classes have different pricing.
keyPoints: Standard, IA, One Zone-IA, and Glacier have different rates
Lower-cost classes trade retrieval time or redundancy
Storage class choice directly impacts monthly bill
examples: Moving infrequently accessed data to S3 Standard-IA
explanation.additionalInfo: Amazon S3 offers multiple storage classes optimized for different access patterns. Choosing the correct class is a primary cost optimization strategy and a frequent exam topic.

explanation.summary: Bucket creation and deletion are free operations.
explanation.why: AWS does not charge for creating or deleting S3 buckets. Charges apply only to stored data and usage.

options.text: The total size in gigabytes of all objects stored.

explanation.summary: S3 pricing is directly based on the total amount of stored data.
examples: Storing 5 TB of backup data in S3
Higher costs when versioning increases stored data
explanation.additionalInfo: Amazon S3 storage pricing is cumulative across all buckets and regions. Features such as versioning and replication increase stored data size and therefore cost.

questions.question: What does the Amazon CloudFront service provide? (Choose TWO)

options.text: Tracks user activity and APl usage.

explanation.summary: CloudFront does not track user activity or API usage.
explanation.why: Tracking user activity and API usage is handled by services such as Amazon CloudWatch, AWS CloudTrail, or Amazon Pinpoint, not CloudFront.

options.text: Increases application availability by caching at the edge.

explanation.summary: Amazon CloudFront improves availability by caching content at edge locations.
keyPoints: Integrates with S3, ALB, and EC2
examples: Serving static website assets from edge locations
Reducing origin load during traffic spikes
explanation.additionalInfo: By caching content at AWS edge locations worldwide, CloudFront reduces dependency on the origin. If the origin becomes temporarily unavailable, cached content can still be served, increasing overall availability. This behavior is commonly tested in AWS exams.

explanation.summary: CloudFront is not a disaster recovery service.
explanation.why: Disaster recovery focuses on data replication, backups, and failover across regions. CloudFront is a content delivery network, not a DR solution.

options.text: Stores archived data at very low costs.

explanation.summary: CloudFront does not provide low-cost archival storage.
explanation.why: Archival storage is provided by services such as Amazon S3 Glacier, not CloudFront.

options.text: Delivers content to end users with low latency.

explanation.summary: CloudFront delivers content globally with low latency.
keyPoints: Uses a global content delivery network
Routes users to nearest edge location
Optimized for static and dynamic content
examples: Serving images and scripts with minimal delay
explanation.additionalInfo: Amazon CloudFront is designed to minimize latency by serving content from the closest possible edge location. This is a core use case and a frequent exam topic when discussing performance optimization.

questions.question: You are facing a lot of problems with your current contact center. Which service provides a cloud-based contact center that can deliver a better service for your customers?

explanation.summary: Amazon Lightsail is a simplified compute service, not a contact center solution.
explanation.why: Lightsail provides virtual servers and basic infrastructure, not customer interaction or call center capabilities.

explanation.summary: Amazon Connect is a fully managed cloud-based contact center service.
explanation.additionalInfo: Amazon Connect allows organizations to quickly deploy a contact center without managing hardware. It supports voice and chat, integrates with CRM systems, and scales based on demand. This service is frequently referenced in AWS exams for customer support use cases.

explanation.summary: AWS Direct Connect provides private network connectivity.
explanation.why: Direct Connect improves network performance and reliability but does not provide contact center functionality.

explanation.summary: Elastic Beanstalk is an application deployment service.
explanation.why: Elastic Beanstalk helps deploy applications but does not offer customer communication or call routing features.

questions.question: You have migrated your application to AWS recently. How can you view the AWS costs applied to your account?

options.text: Using the AWS Cost & Usage Report.

explanation.summary: The AWS Cost & Usage Report provides detailed billing information.
keyPoints: Used for cost analysis and reporting
explanation.additionalInfo: The Cost & Usage Report delivers comprehensive billing data at an hourly or daily granularity. It is commonly used for chargeback, forecasting, and cost optimization strategies.

options.text: Using the AWS Total Cost of Ownership (TCO) dashboard.

explanation.summary: The TCO calculator estimates savings, not actual AWS charges.
explanation.why: The TCO tool compares on-premises costs to AWS but does not display real billing data.

options.text: Using the AWS CloudWatch logs dashboard.

explanation.summary: CloudWatch Logs monitor applications, not billing.
explanation.why: CloudWatch provides metrics and logs but does not report account-level costs.

explanation.summary: The VPC dashboard manages networking resources.
explanation.why: Amazon VPC dashboards do not provide billing or cost visibility.

questions.question: Which of the following are valid Amazon EC2 Reserved Instance types? (Choose TWO)

explanation.summary: Convertible Reserved Instances are a valid EC2 Reserved Instance type.
keyPoints: Allows instance family and type changes
Provides lower discount than Standard RIs
Can be exchanged during the term
examples: Switching instance families as application requirements evolve
Maintaining RI discounts while migrating workloads
explanation.additionalInfo: Convertible Reserved Instances provide flexibility by allowing exchanges to different instance families, operating systems, or tenancy, provided the new configuration has equal or greater value. This flexibility comes at the cost of a lower discount compared to Standard Reserved Instances, making them ideal for workloads with uncertain future requirements.

explanation.summary: Expedited is not an EC2 Reserved Instance type.
explanation.why: AWS does not offer an EC2 Reserved Instance category called Expedited. This term is commonly used as a distractor in exams.

explanation.summary: Bulk is not a valid EC2 Reserved Instance type.
explanation.why: AWS pricing models do not include Bulk Reserved Instances. Valid types are Standard and Convertible.

explanation.summary: Spot Instances are a separate purchasing option, not Reserved Instances.
explanation.why: Spot Instances use spare AWS capacity with variable pricing and interruption risk. They are not a Reserved Instance type.

explanation.summary: Standard Reserved Instances are a valid EC2 Reserved Instance type.
keyPoints: Provide highest discount compared to On-Demand
examples: Reducing EC2 costs for predictable usage
explanation.additionalInfo: Standard Reserved Instances offer the largest savings in exchange for less flexibility. Instance attributes such as family, size, region, and tenancy are fixed for the duration of the reservation, making them best suited for predictable workloads.

questions.question: Which of the following services gives you access to all AWS auditor-issued reports and certifications?

explanation.summary: AWS Artifact provides on-demand access to AWS compliance reports and certifications.
keyPoints: Provides SOC, ISO, and PCI reports
Accessible from the AWS Management Console
examples: Downloading SOC 2 reports for compliance audits
Accessing ISO certifications for regulatory reviews
explanation.additionalInfo: AWS Artifact allows customers to self-serve compliance documentation without engaging AWS Support. This service is frequently tested in AWS exams when discussing audits, compliance, and governance.

explanation.summary: AWS Config tracks resource configuration changes.
explanation.why: AWS Config monitors configuration compliance but does not provide AWS-issued audit reports or certifications.

explanation.summary: CloudWatch is used for monitoring and logging.
explanation.why: CloudWatch provides metrics and logs, not compliance documentation.

explanation.summary: CloudTrail records API activity.
explanation.why: CloudTrail provides audit logs of account activity, not AWS compliance certifications.

questions.question: You manage a blog on AWS that has different environments: development, testing, and production. What can you use to create a custom console for each environment to view and manage your resources easily?

explanation.summary: AWS Resource Groups allow logical grouping of resources for easier management.
keyPoints: Creates custom views in the console
examples: Grouping production EC2 and RDS resources
Creating separate views for dev and test environments
explanation.additionalInfo: AWS Resource Groups enable teams to manage resources by environment, application, or workload. They rely on tagging strategies and are commonly used to simplify operations in multi-environment architectures, a frequent scenario in AWS exams.

explanation.summary: Placement Groups control EC2 instance placement.
explanation.why: Placement Groups affect network latency and fault tolerance but do not create console views or manage environments.

explanation.summary: The AWS Management Console is the main interface, not an environment-specific organizer.
explanation.why: While the console provides access to services, it does not create custom environment groupings without Resource Groups.

explanation.summary: Tag Editor manages tags but does not create custom consoles.
explanation.why: Tag Editor is used to search and modify tags, not to build environment-based console views.

questions.question: Which AWS service collects metrics from running EC2 instances?

explanation.summary: Amazon Inspector focuses on security assessments, not metric collection.
explanation.why: Inspector evaluates EC2 instances for vulnerabilities and security best practices. It does not collect performance or operational metrics such as CPU or memory usage.

explanation.summary: Amazon CloudWatch collects and monitors metrics from EC2 instances.
keyPoints: Collects CPU, network, disk, and status metrics
examples: Triggering Auto Scaling based on metrics
explanation.additionalInfo: CloudWatch is the primary monitoring service in AWS. EC2 instances automatically publish basic metrics to CloudWatch, while detailed monitoring can be enabled for higher resolution data. CloudWatch metrics are widely used in exam questions related to monitoring and scaling.

explanation.summary: CloudFormation is an infrastructure provisioning service.
explanation.why: CloudFormation creates and manages AWS resources using templates but does not monitor or collect metrics from running instances.

explanation.summary: CloudTrail records API activity, not performance metrics.
explanation.why: CloudTrail logs who did what and when in an AWS account, which is useful for auditing but not for system monitoring.

questions.question: Your web application currently faces performance issues and suffers from long load times. Which of the following AWS services could help fix these issues and improve performance?

explanation.summary: Amazon Detective is used for security investigations.
explanation.why: Detective analyzes security-related data to investigate potential threats. It does not diagnose or improve application performance.

explanation.summary: AWS X-Ray helps analyze and improve application performance.
keyPoints: Integrates with EC2, Lambda, and ECS
explanation.additionalInfo: AWS X-Ray provides distributed tracing, which is essential for understanding performance issues in microservices and serverless architectures. It helps developers pinpoint where delays occur, making it a common exam answer for performance troubleshooting scenarios.

explanation.summary: AWS Security Hub centralizes security findings.
explanation.why: Security Hub aggregates security alerts and compliance checks but does not address application performance or latency issues.

explanation.summary: AWS Shield protects against DDoS attacks.
explanation.why: Shield improves availability during attacks but does not analyze or optimize application performance under normal conditions.

questions.question: Which of the following compute resources are serverless? (Choose TWO)

explanation.summary: Amazon EC2 requires server management.
explanation.why: With EC2, customers are responsible for managing the operating system, patching, and instance lifecycle, which disqualifies it as serverless.

explanation.summary: AWS Fargate is a serverless compute engine for containers.
examples: Running containerized workloads without managing EC2
explanation.additionalInfo: AWS Fargate abstracts the underlying infrastructure, allowing developers to focus on containers rather than servers. It is classified as serverless because customers do not manage the compute instances.

explanation.summary: AWS Lambda is a fully serverless compute service.
explanation.additionalInfo: AWS Lambda is the most common example of serverless computing in AWS exams. Customers upload code and AWS handles all infrastructure, scaling, and availability.

explanation.summary: Amazon ECS is a container orchestration service.
explanation.why: ECS can be serverless only when combined with Fargate. On its own, ECS requires EC2 instances and is not inherently serverless.

explanation.summary: Amazon EMR requires cluster management.
explanation.why: EMR runs on EC2 or EKS clusters that must be managed, making it a managed service but not serverless.

questions.question: For compliance and regulatory purposes, a government agency requires that their applications must run on hardware that is dedicated to them only. How can you meet this requirement?

explanation.summary: EC2 Dedicated Hosts provide physical servers dedicated to a single customer.
keyPoints: Visibility into sockets, cores, and host IDs
explanation.additionalInfo: EC2 Dedicated Hosts allow customers to use a physical server fully dedicated to their use. This satisfies compliance requirements where shared tenancy is not permitted. Dedicated Hosts also help with per-socket or per-core licensing models, making them a frequent exam answer for compliance-focused scenarios.

explanation.summary: Reserved Instances are a pricing model, not a tenancy model.
explanation.why: Reserved Instances provide billing discounts but do not guarantee dedicated physical hardware.

explanation.summary: Spot Instances use spare capacity and are not dedicated.
explanation.why: Spot Instances can be interrupted and run on shared infrastructure, making them unsuitable for compliance requirements.

explanation.summary: On-Demand Instances do not guarantee dedicated hardware.
explanation.why: On-Demand Instances run on shared hardware unless combined with Dedicated Hosts or Dedicated Instances.

questions.question: Which AWS Cost Governance best practice recommends refining workloads regularly to make the most of existing AWS resources and reduce costs?

explanation.summary: Tagging enforcement focuses on cost allocation, not workload optimization.
explanation.why: Tags help categorize and track costs but do not directly reduce them by optimizing resource usage.

explanation.summary: Architecture Optimization focuses on continuously refining workloads for cost efficiency.
examples: Switching to managed services for lower cost
explanation.additionalInfo: Architecture Optimization is a key AWS cost governance practice that emphasizes iterative improvement. By regularly reviewing workloads, organizations can take advantage of new AWS services, instance types, and pricing models to reduce costs. This concept aligns closely with the Cost Optimization pillar of the AWS Well-Architected Framework.

explanation.summary: Budgeting tracks and forecasts costs.
explanation.why: Budgeting provides visibility and alerts but does not directly optimize resource usage.

explanation.summary: Resource controls limit provisioning.
explanation.why: Resource controls prevent overspending but do not focus on refining existing workloads.

questions.question: An organization needs to build a financial application that requires support for ACID transactions. Which AWS database service is most appropriate in this case?

explanation.summary: Amazon Redshift is optimized for analytics, not transactions.
explanation.why: Redshift is a data warehouse designed for OLAP workloads and does not support transactional ACID workloads.

explanation.summary: Amazon RDS supports ACID-compliant relational databases.
keyPoints: Supports MySQL, PostgreSQL, Oracle, and SQL Server
explanation.additionalInfo: Amazon RDS is designed for OLTP workloads that require strong consistency and transactional guarantees. It supports ACID properties through relational database engines, making it the correct choice for financial applications in AWS exams.

explanation.summary: CloudHSM manages encryption keys.
explanation.why: CloudHSM provides hardware security modules and is not a database service.

explanation.summary: AWS DMS is used for database migration.
explanation.why: DMS migrates databases but does not host or run transactional workloads.

questions.question: What can you use to assign permissions directly to an IAM user?

explanation.summary: IAM Identity is a general concept, not a permission mechanism.
explanation.why: IAM identities include users, groups, and roles, but permissions themselves are not assigned using an identity object.

explanation.summary: IAM Groups assign permissions indirectly.
explanation.why: Groups attach policies to multiple users, but the question asks for assigning permissions directly to a user.

explanation.summary: IAM Roles provide temporary permissions.
explanation.why: Roles are assumed by users or services and are not directly attached to IAM users for permanent permissions.

explanation.summary: IAM Policies define permissions and can be attached directly to users.
keyPoints: Can be attached directly to IAM users
examples: Attaching an S3 read-only policy to a user
Granting EC2 start and stop permissions
explanation.additionalInfo: IAM policies are the fundamental mechanism for granting permissions in AWS. Policies can be attached directly to users, groups, or roles. Attaching policies directly to users should be done sparingly in favor of groups, but it is fully supported and often tested in exams.

questions.question: The owner of an E-Commerce application notices that the compute capacity requirements vary heavily from time to time. What makes AWS more economical than traditional data centers for this type of application?

options.text: AWS allows customers to launch powerful EC2 instances to handle spikes in load.

explanation.summary: Instance power alone does not reduce cost.
explanation.why: Launching powerful instances can actually increase costs if they run continuously.

options.text: AWS allows customers to pay upfront to get bigger discounts.

explanation.summary: Upfront payments are optional, not the key benefit here.
explanation.why: The primary advantage is elasticity, not upfront discount models.

options.text: AWS allows customers to launch and terminate EC2 instances based on demand.

explanation.summary: Elasticity allows customers to match capacity with demand.
keyPoints: Scale resources up and down dynamically
Pay only for what you use
No need to provision for peak capacity
explanation.additionalInfo: Elasticity is one of the fundamental advantages of cloud computing. Unlike traditional data centers that require provisioning for peak load, AWS allows dynamic scaling so customers pay only for actual usage. This concept is heavily tested in AWS exams.

options.text: AWS allows customers to choose cheaper types of EC2 instances that best fit their needs.

explanation.summary: Instance choice matters but is not the main economic driver.
explanation.why: While right-sizing helps, the key advantage described is elasticity, not instance selection.

questions.question: Amazon RDS supports multiple database engines to choose from. Which of the following is not one of them?

explanation.summary: PostgreSQL is a supported Amazon RDS engine.
explanation.why: Amazon RDS fully supports PostgreSQL as a managed relational database engine.

explanation.summary: Oracle Database is supported by Amazon RDS.
explanation.why: RDS offers managed Oracle Database with multiple editions.

explanation.summary: Microsoft SQL Server is supported by Amazon RDS.
explanation.why: Amazon RDS provides managed SQL Server deployments.

explanation.summary: Teradata is not an Amazon RDS supported engine.
keyPoints: Not offered as a managed RDS engine
Typically deployed on EC2 or via partner solutions
explanation.additionalInfo: Amazon RDS supports engines such as MySQL, PostgreSQL, MariaDB, Oracle, SQL Server, and Amazon Aurora. Teradata is an enterprise data warehouse platform and is not available as an RDS managed engine, making it the correct answer.

questions.question: Which of the following AWS services would help you migrate on-premise databases to AWS?

explanation.summary: AWS Database Migration Service helps migrate databases to AWS with minimal downtime.
keyPoints: Keeps source database operational during migration
Works with on-premises and cloud databases
Commonly used for lift-and-shift database migrations
examples: Migrating an on-premises Oracle database to Amazon RDS
Replicating MySQL data from on-premises to AWS
explanation.additionalInfo: AWS DMS is purpose-built for database migration scenarios. It allows organizations to migrate databases to AWS quickly and securely while keeping the source database online. This service is frequently tested in AWS exams for migration use cases.

explanation.summary: S3 Transfer Acceleration speeds up object uploads.
explanation.why: It is used to accelerate file transfers to S3, not database migrations.

explanation.summary: AWS Directory Service manages directories.
explanation.why: It provides Active Directory functionality and does not migrate databases.

explanation.summary: Transit Gateway connects networks.
explanation.why: It manages network connectivity but does not migrate databases.

questions.question: For new AWS customers, what is the EASIEST way to launch a simple WordPress website on AWS?

options.text: Run WordPress on an Amazon Lightsail instance.

explanation.summary: Amazon Lightsail provides preconfigured WordPress instances.
examples: Launching a blog with a few clicks
explanation.additionalInfo: Amazon Lightsail is designed for users who want to get started quickly without managing complex infrastructure. It offers WordPress blueprints that handle setup automatically, making it the easiest option for new AWS customers.

options.text: Install WordPress on an Amazon EC2 instance.

explanation.summary: Manual EC2 setup requires more configuration.
explanation.why: Installing WordPress on EC2 involves OS management, web server configuration, and database setup, making it more complex.

options.text: Use the Amazon S3 Web hosting feature.

explanation.summary: S3 static hosting does not support WordPress.
explanation.why: WordPress requires a server-side runtime and database, which S3 static hosting cannot provide.

options.text: Host the website directly on AWS Cloud Development Kit (AWS CDK).

explanation.summary: AWS CDK is an infrastructure as code tool.
explanation.why: CDK defines cloud infrastructure and does not directly host or run WordPress applications.

questions.question: Which of the following would you use to manage your encryption keys in the AWS Cloud? (Choose TWO)

explanation.summary: AWS Key Management Service manages and controls encryption keys.
explanation.additionalInfo: AWS KMS is the primary service for managing encryption keys in AWS. It integrates with most AWS services and supports audit logging through CloudTrail, making it a core exam topic.

explanation.summary: AWS Certificate Manager manages SSL/TLS certificates.
explanation.why: ACM manages certificates, not general-purpose encryption keys for data-at-rest or application encryption.

explanation.summary: CodeDeploy automates application deployments.
explanation.why: It is unrelated to encryption or key management.

explanation.summary: CodeCommit stores source code.
explanation.why: It does not provide encryption key management.

explanation.summary: CloudHSM provides customer-controlled hardware security modules.
examples: Managing keys with full customer control
explanation.additionalInfo: AWS CloudHSM is used when customers require full control over encryption keys and hardware. It is commonly compared with KMS in exams to test understanding of shared responsibility and compliance needs.

questions.question: Which of the following services allows you to install and run custom relational database software?

explanation.summary: Amazon EC2 provides full control over the operating system and installed software.
explanation.additionalInfo: Amazon EC2 is the correct choice when customers need to install and manage their own database software. Unlike Amazon RDS, EC2 gives full control over the OS, database binaries, and configuration. This distinction is frequently tested in AWS exams.

explanation.summary: Amazon Cognito manages user authentication.
explanation.why: Cognito provides identity management and does not host or run databases.

explanation.summary: Amazon RDS restricts direct database software installation.
explanation.why: RDS is a managed service and does not allow installing custom database engines or modifying underlying OS software.

explanation.summary: Amazon Inspector performs security assessments.
explanation.why: Inspector evaluates vulnerabilities and does not provide compute or database hosting capabilities.

questions.question: Your application requirements for CPU and RAM are changing in an unpredictable way. Which service can be used to dynamically adjust these resources based on load?

explanation.summary: Auto Scaling dynamically adjusts compute capacity based on demand.
examples: Scaling web servers during traffic spikes
explanation.additionalInfo: AWS Auto Scaling enables applications to handle variable workloads by adjusting the number of instances automatically. This elasticity ensures performance while controlling costs and is a core AWS exam concept.

explanation.summary: Elastic Load Balancing distributes traffic.
explanation.why: ELB routes requests but does not scale compute resources.

explanation.summary: Route 53 provides DNS services.
explanation.why: DNS routing does not adjust CPU or RAM resources.

explanation.summary: Amazon ECS orchestrates containers.
explanation.why: ECS manages containers but does not directly scale underlying compute resources unless combined with Auto Scaling or Fargate.

questions.question: A company has infrastructure hosted in an on-premises data center. They currently have an operations team that takes care of identity management. If they decide to migrate to the AWS cloud, which of the following services would help them perform the same role in AWS?

explanation.summary: AWS Identity and Access Management manages users and permissions.
examples: Managing user access to AWS services
explanation.additionalInfo: AWS IAM replaces on-premises identity management systems by controlling authentication and authorization for AWS resources. It integrates with external identity providers and is a fundamental AWS service tested frequently in exams.

explanation.summary: AWS Outposts extends AWS infrastructure on-premises.
explanation.why: Outposts provides hardware and services, not identity management.

explanation.summary: Federation enables single sign-on.
explanation.why: Federation integrates identities but does not replace IAM as the core identity service.

explanation.summary: Amazon Redshift is a data warehouse service.
explanation.why: Redshift does not provide identity or access management capabilities.

questions.question: What are some key design principles for designing public cloud systems? (Choose TWO)

options.text: Reserved capacity instead of on demand.

explanation.summary: Reserved capacity limits flexibility in cloud environments.
explanation.why: Public cloud design emphasizes elasticity and on-demand provisioning rather than fixed reserved capacity.

explanation.summary: Loose coupling improves scalability and resilience.
explanation.additionalInfo: Loose coupling allows cloud systems to evolve and scale independently. AWS promotes this principle heavily in architecture and exam questions, especially when discussing resilience and scalability.

explanation.summary: Managed services reduce operational overhead.
explanation.why: Public cloud best practices favor managed services to reduce maintenance and improve reliability.

options.text: Disposable resources instead of fixed servers.

explanation.summary: Disposable resources enable automation and resilience.
examples: Replacing failed instances instead of repairing them
explanation.additionalInfo: Designing systems with disposable resources allows failures to be handled automatically. AWS recommends replacing failed components rather than fixing them, a principle frequently tested in exams.

options.text: Multi-AZ deployments instead of multi-region deployments.

explanation.summary: Multi-region deployments are often preferred for resilience.
explanation.why: Public cloud design principles emphasize choosing the appropriate scope. Multi-AZ is common, but multi-region is often used for higher fault tolerance.

questions.question: Where can AWS account owners get a list of all users in their account, including the status of their AWS credentials?

explanation.summary: CloudTrail records API activity.
explanation.why: CloudTrail logs actions but does not provide a consolidated credential status report.

explanation.summary: The IAM Credential Report lists all IAM users and credential status.
keyPoints: Shows password and access key status
explanation.additionalInfo: The IAM Credential Report is essential for security audits. It provides a snapshot of all IAM users and their credential usage, helping organizations identify unused or risky credentials.

explanation.summary: AWS Artifact provides compliance reports.
explanation.why: Artifact contains AWS-issued audit documents, not IAM user credential details.

explanation.summary: The Cost and Usage Report provides billing data.
explanation.why: It does not include IAM user or credential information.

questions.question: Which of the following services enables you to easily generate and use your own encryption keys in the AWS Cloud?

explanation.summary: AWS Shield protects against DDoS attacks.
explanation.why: Shield provides DDoS protection and does not manage encryption keys.

explanation.summary: AWS Certificate Manager manages SSL/TLS certificates.
explanation.why: ACM manages certificates rather than general-purpose encryption keys.

explanation.summary: AWS CloudHSM allows customers to generate and control their own encryption keys.
examples: Using customer-managed keys for sensitive workloads
explanation.additionalInfo: CloudHSM is designed for customers who require complete control over encryption keys and hardware. It contrasts with AWS KMS, which is managed by AWS. This distinction is frequently tested in exams.

explanation.summary: AWS WAF protects web applications.
explanation.why: WAF filters malicious traffic and does not provide encryption key management.

questions.question: You have developed a web application targeting a global audience. Which of the following will help you achieve the highest redundancy and fault tolerance from an infrastructure perspective?

options.text: There is no need to architect for these capabilities in AWS, as AWS is redundant by default.

explanation.summary: AWS provides highly available infrastructure, but architecture decisions still matter.
explanation.why: Customers are responsible for architecting applications for fault tolerance. AWS does not automatically make applications highly available across regions.

options.text: Deploy the application in a single Availability Zone.

explanation.summary: A single Availability Zone is a single point of failure.
explanation.why: Deploying in one AZ does not protect against AZ-level failures and does not provide high fault tolerance.

options.text: Deploy the application in multiple Availability Zones in a single AWS region.

explanation.summary: Multi-AZ deployments improve availability but not maximum fault tolerance.
explanation.why: While Multi-AZ protects against AZ failures, it does not protect against regional outages.

options.text: Deploy the application in muitiple Availability Zones in multiple AWS regions.

explanation.summary: Multi-region, multi-AZ deployments provide the highest level of redundancy and fault tolerance.
examples: Failing over traffic during regional outages
explanation.additionalInfo: Deploying across multiple Availability Zones and multiple AWS regions provides the strongest protection against failures. This approach is commonly referenced in AWS exams when maximum availability and fault tolerance are required.

questions.question: For some services, AWS automatically replicates data across multiple Availability Zones to provide fault tolerance in the event of a server failure or Availability Zone outage. Select TWO services that automatically replicate data across Availability Zones.

explanation.summary: Instance Store data is tied to a single instance.
explanation.why: Instance Store does not replicate data and data is lost if the instance stops or fails.

explanation.summary: Amazon S3 automatically replicates data across multiple Availability Zones.
explanation.additionalInfo: Amazon S3 automatically stores data redundantly across multiple AZs within a region. This behavior is built-in and does not require user configuration, making S3 a frequent exam answer for durability and fault tolerance questions.

explanation.summary: Amazon DynamoDB automatically replicates data across Availability Zones.
explanation.additionalInfo: DynamoDB is a regional service that automatically replicates data across multiple AZs. This ensures high availability and durability without customer intervention, a key distinction often tested in exams.

explanation.summary: Route 53 is a DNS service.
explanation.why: Route 53 manages DNS routing and health checks, not data storage replication.

explanation.summary: AWS VPN provides secure network connectivity.
explanation.why: VPN services do not replicate application data.

questions.question: Which of the following factors affect Amazon CloudFront cost? (Choose TWO)

explanation.summary: CloudFront pricing includes charges per request.
keyPoints: Charged per HTTP and HTTPS request
explanation.additionalInfo: Amazon CloudFront charges based on the number of requests served and data transferred. Requests are a direct cost component and frequently tested in AWS pricing questions.

explanation.summary: Traffic distribution affects CloudFront pricing.
keyPoints: Pricing varies by edge location region
explanation.additionalInfo: CloudFront pricing differs by geographic region. Traffic served from certain regions incurs higher costs, making traffic distribution a key pricing consideration.

explanation.summary: CloudFront does not use volumes.
explanation.why: Volumes relate to block storage services like EBS, not CDN services.

explanation.summary: CloudFront is a managed service without instance types.
explanation.why: Customers do not choose instance types when using CloudFront.

explanation.summary: Storage classes apply to S3, not CloudFront.
explanation.why: CloudFront pricing does not depend on S3 storage class.

questions.question: Which of the following resources can an AWS customer use to learn more about prohibited uses of the services offered by AWS?

explanation.summary: Service Control Policies enforce permissions, not usage rules.
explanation.why: SCPs restrict actions within AWS Organizations but do not document prohibited service usage.

explanation.summary: AWS Artifact provides compliance reports.
explanation.why: Artifact contains audit and compliance documents, not acceptable use guidelines.

explanation.summary: AWS Budgets track and alert on costs.
explanation.why: Budgets help manage spending and do not define prohibited service usage.

explanation.summary: The AWS Acceptable Use Policy defines prohibited uses of AWS services.
examples: Rules against abusive or harmful activities
explanation.additionalInfo: The AWS Acceptable Use Policy specifies what customers are not allowed to do when using AWS services. Understanding this policy is important for compliance and governance scenarios in AWS exams.

questions.question: Which of the following security resources are available to any user for free? (Choose TWO)

explanation.summary: AWS Bulletins provide public security announcements.
examples: Staying informed on AWS security updates
explanation.additionalInfo: AWS Bulletins publish important security information and notifications. They are freely available and do not require an AWS Support plan.

explanation.summary: Technical Account Managers are a paid service.
explanation.why: TAM access is included only with Enterprise Support plans.

explanation.summary: The AWS Support API requires a paid support plan.
explanation.why: Access to the Support API is available only with Business or Enterprise support plans.

explanation.summary: The AWS Security Blog is a free educational resource.
examples: Learning about new AWS security services
explanation.additionalInfo: The AWS Security Blog is maintained by AWS security experts and provides insights into best practices and new features. It is freely accessible to all users.

explanation.summary: Classroom training typically incurs a cost.
explanation.why: Instructor-led training courses are usually paid offerings.

questions.question: How can you protect data stored on Amazon S3 from accidental deletion?

explanation.summary: S3 Versioning protects objects from accidental deletion or overwrite.
examples: Rolling back to a previous object version
explanation.additionalInfo: When S3 Versioning is enabled, deleted objects are marked with a delete marker instead of being permanently removed. This allows data recovery and is a common AWS exam topic for data protection questions.

explanation.summary: Bucket policies control access, not deletion recovery.
explanation.why: Bucket policies define permissions but do not retain deleted data.

explanation.summary: Lifecycle policies manage object transitions and expiration.
explanation.why: Lifecycle policies can delete objects automatically and do not prevent accidental deletion.

explanation.summary: Disabling CRR does not protect against deletion.
explanation.why: CRR affects replication behavior and does not prevent object deletion.

questions.question: Which of the following is the responsibility of AWS according to the AWS Shared Responsibility Model?

explanation.summary: AWS is responsible for securing the underlying global infrastructure.
keyPoints: Protection of regions and edge locations
Part of security of the cloud
explanation.additionalInfo: Under the AWS Shared Responsibility Model, AWS is responsible for security of the cloud, which includes physical infrastructure such as regions, Availability Zones, and edge locations. Customers are responsible for security in the cloud.

explanation.summary: Auditing customer environments is not AWS responsibility.
explanation.why: Customers are responsible for auditing their own applications and resource usage.

explanation.summary: Monitoring usage is a customer responsibility.
explanation.why: Customers must configure and monitor services such as CloudWatch for their workloads.

explanation.summary: Customers are responsible for access management.
explanation.why: IAM configuration, user access, and permissions are customer responsibilities.

questions.question: Which of the following AWS support plans provides access to only the seven core AWS Trusted Advisor checks?

explanation.summary: Business and Enterprise provide full Trusted Advisor checks.
explanation.why: These plans include the full set of Trusted Advisor checks, not only the core seven.

explanation.summary: Basic and Developer plans include only the core Trusted Advisor checks.
explanation.additionalInfo: The Basic and Developer AWS Support plans provide access to the seven core Trusted Advisor checks. Full checks are available only with Business and Enterprise support plans.

explanation.summary: Enterprise Support provides full Trusted Advisor access.
explanation.why: Enterprise includes the complete set of Trusted Advisor checks.

explanation.summary: Business Support provides full Trusted Advisor checks.
explanation.why: Business support includes full Trusted Advisor functionality.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a benefit of using AWS Lambda?

options.text: AWS Lambda runs code without provisioning or managing servers.

explanation.summary: This is a core benefit of AWS Lambda.
explanation.why: Lambda abstracts server management entirely.

options.text: AWS Lambda provides resizable compute capacity in the cloud.

explanation.summary: Lambda does not provide resizable compute capacity.
keyPoints: Compute size is selected per function
Scaling is automatic, not manually resized
examples: Selecting memory size for a Lambda function
explanation.additionalInfo: AWS Lambda automatically scales based on the number of requests but does not provide resizable compute capacity like EC2. Customers configure memory, which indirectly affects CPU allocation, but cannot resize instances dynamically.

options.text: There is no charge when your AWS Lambda code is not running.

explanation.summary: This is a key benefit of AWS Lambda.
explanation.why: Lambda charges only for execution time and number of requests.

options.text: AWS Lambda can be called directly from any mobile app.

explanation.summary: Lambda can be invoked via APIs and SDKs.
explanation.why: Lambda functions can be exposed through API Gateway and invoked by mobile applications.

questions.question: How does AWS help customers achieve compliance in the cloud?

options.text: It's not possible to meet regulatory compliance requirements in the Cloud.

explanation.summary: AWS supports compliance with many regulatory standards.
explanation.why: AWS provides compliant infrastructure and services that help customers meet regulatory requirements.

options.text: AWS applies the most common Cloud security standards, and is responsible for complying with customers' applicable laws and regulations.

explanation.summary: Customers retain responsibility for their own compliance obligations.
explanation.why: AWS provides compliant infrastructure, but customers are responsible for complying with applicable laws and regulations.

options.text: AWS has many common assurance certifications such as ISO 9001 and HIPAA.

explanation.summary: AWS certifications alone do not ensure customer compliance.
explanation.why: Certifications support compliance efforts but do not fully define how AWS helps customers meet regulatory requirements.

options.text: Many AWS services are assessed regularly to comply with local laws and regulations.

explanation.summary: AWS regularly assesses services to meet compliance requirements.
examples: Using AWS services for HIPAA workloads
explanation.additionalInfo: AWS undergoes regular independent audits to validate compliance with numerous standards and regulations. Customers can leverage these assessments to build compliant workloads while maintaining responsibility for their applications and data.

questions.question: Who is responsible for scaling a DynamoDB database in the AWS Shared Responsibility Model?

explanation.summary: Security teams do not manage database scaling.
explanation.why: Scaling DynamoDB capacity is handled by the service itself.

explanation.summary: Developers do not manually scale DynamoDB infrastructure.
explanation.why: DynamoDB is a fully managed service with automatic scaling capabilities.

explanation.summary: AWS manages DynamoDB scaling automatically.
examples: Scaling read and write capacity automatically
explanation.additionalInfo: Under the AWS Shared Responsibility Model, AWS manages the infrastructure and scaling of DynamoDB. Customers configure capacity modes but do not manage servers or scaling logic.

explanation.summary: DevOps teams do not scale DynamoDB infrastructure.
explanation.why: AWS abstracts all infrastructure management for DynamoDB.

questions.question: You are working as a web app developer. You are currently facing issues in media playback for mobile devices because your media format is not supported. Which of the following AWS services can help you convert your media into another format?

explanation.summary: Amazon Elastic Transcoder converts media files into different formats.
keyPoints: Supports common video and audio formats
explanation.additionalInfo: Amazon Elastic Transcoder is designed to convert media files stored in S3 into formats suitable for playback on various devices. Although newer services exist, Elastic Transcoder remains a valid exam topic.

explanation.summary: Amazon Pinpoint handles user engagement and messaging.
explanation.why: Pinpoint does not process or convert media formats.

explanation.summary: Amazon S3 stores objects.
explanation.why: S3 provides storage and does not convert media formats.

explanation.summary: Amazon Rekognition analyzes images and video.
explanation.why: Rekognition performs content analysis, not format conversion.

questions.question: What are the benefits of the AWS Organizations service? (Choose TWO)

explanation.summary: AWS Organizations enables centralized access control across accounts.
examples: Restricting use of specific AWS services
explanation.additionalInfo: AWS Organizations allows administrators to define Service Control Policies that control which AWS services and actions are permitted across member accounts. This is a core governance benefit frequently tested in exams.

options.text: Help organizations design and maintain an accelerated path to successful cloud adoption.

explanation.summary: This describes the AWS Cloud Adoption Framework.
explanation.why: AWS Organizations focuses on account management and governance, not cloud adoption strategy.

explanation.summary: Payment methods are managed at the payer account level.
explanation.why: AWS Organizations supports consolidated billing but does not manage payment methods directly.

options.text: Help organization achieve their desired business outcomes with AWS.

explanation.summary: This is not a specific AWS Organizations feature.
explanation.why: This statement is too broad and aligns more with consulting or advisory services.

options.text: Consolidate billing across multiple AWS accounts.

explanation.summary: AWS Organizations enables consolidated billing.
explanation.additionalInfo: Consolidated billing allows organizations to combine usage across accounts, enabling volume discounts and simpler cost management. This is one of the primary benefits of AWS Organizations and is commonly tested in exams.

questions.question: Which AWS service allows you to build a data warehouse in the cloud?

explanation.summary: AWS Shield provides DDoS protection.
explanation.why: Shield protects against attacks and does not store or analyze data.

explanation.summary: Amazon Redshift is a fully managed cloud data warehouse.
explanation.additionalInfo: Amazon Redshift is AWS’s primary data warehouse service, optimized for analytical queries and large-scale data processing. It is a standard exam answer for data warehousing scenarios.

explanation.summary: Amazon RDS is designed for transactional databases.
explanation.why: RDS supports OLTP workloads and is not optimized for large-scale analytics.

explanation.summary: Amazon Comprehend is a natural language processing service.
explanation.why: It analyzes text data but does not provide data warehouse capabilities.

questions.question: What AWS service allows you to buy third-party software solutions and services that run on AWS resources?

explanation.summary: Application Discovery Service identifies on-premises workloads.
explanation.why: It assists with migration planning and does not sell software solutions.

explanation.summary: Amazon DevPay is deprecated.
explanation.why: DevPay is no longer the mechanism for purchasing third-party software on AWS.

explanation.summary: AWS Marketplace provides third-party software solutions.
explanation.additionalInfo: AWS Marketplace allows customers to find, buy, and deploy third-party software that runs on AWS. Charges are included directly in the AWS bill, simplifying procurement and licensing.

explanation.summary: Resource Groups organize AWS resources.
explanation.why: They do not provide access to third-party software marketplaces.

questions.question: Which of the following services is an AWS repository management system that allows for storing, versioning, and managing your application code?

explanation.summary: AWS CodePipeline orchestrates CI/CD workflows.
explanation.why: CodePipeline coordinates build, test, and deploy stages but does not store source code.

explanation.summary: AWS CodeCommit is a managed source control service.
explanation.additionalInfo: AWS CodeCommit provides secure, scalable Git-based repositories without the need to manage infrastructure. It integrates with other AWS DevOps services and is frequently tested in exam questions related to CI/CD.

explanation.summary: AWS X-Ray is used for application tracing.
explanation.why: X-Ray analyzes application performance and does not store source code.

explanation.summary: Amazon Inspector performs security assessments.
explanation.why: Inspector evaluates vulnerabilities and does not manage source code repositories.

questions.question: Which AWS service can be used to route end users to the nearest AWS Region to reduce latency?

explanation.summary: Amazon Cognito handles authentication.
explanation.why: Cognito manages user identities and does not perform traffic routing.

explanation.summary: Systems Manager manages infrastructure operations.
explanation.why: It does not route user traffic across regions.

explanation.summary: AWS Cloud9 is an IDE service.
explanation.why: Cloud9 provides development environments, not traffic routing.

explanation.summary: Amazon Route 53 routes users based on latency.
examples: Routing users to nearest regional endpoint
Improving response times for global users
explanation.additionalInfo: Amazon Route 53 supports latency-based routing, allowing traffic to be directed to the AWS Region that provides the lowest latency for users. This is a common exam topic for global application design.

questions.question: Which feature enables users to sign into their AWS accounts with their existing corporate credentials?

explanation.summary: Federation allows users to access AWS using existing identities.
examples: Logging in with Active Directory credentials
explanation.additionalInfo: Federation enables AWS access using external identity providers such as Active Directory or SAML-based systems. This allows organizations to reuse existing credentials while maintaining centralized access control.

explanation.summary: Access keys are static credentials.
explanation.why: Access keys are used for programmatic access and do not enable SSO with corporate credentials.

explanation.summary: IAM permissions define allowed actions.
explanation.why: Permissions do not handle authentication or identity federation.

explanation.summary: WAF rules filter web traffic.
explanation.why: WAF protects applications and does not provide authentication mechanisms.

questions.question: According to the AWS shared responsibility model, what are the controls that customers fully inherit from AWS? (Choose TWO)

explanation.summary: Training and awareness remain a customer responsibility.
explanation.why: Customers are responsible for ensuring their staff are trained on security and compliance.

explanation.summary: Communications controls are shared, not fully inherited.
explanation.why: Customers still configure network access and communication policies.

explanation.summary: Physical data center security is fully managed by AWS.
explanation.additionalInfo: AWS customers fully inherit physical data center security controls. These controls are implemented and maintained entirely by AWS and require no customer action.

explanation.summary: Environmental protections are fully handled by AWS.
explanation.additionalInfo: Environmental controls such as power, cooling, and fire suppression are fully inherited from AWS. Customers rely on AWS to manage these aspects of physical infrastructure security.

explanation.summary: Resource configuration is a customer responsibility.
explanation.why: Customers must configure their AWS resources securely and appropriately.

questions.question: What can you access by visiting the URL: [http://status.aws.amazon.com](http://status.aws.amazon.com)?

explanation.summary: Billing dashboards are accessed through the AWS Management Console.
explanation.why: The status page does not show billing information.

explanation.summary: Cost dashboards provide cost analysis.
explanation.why: The AWS status page does not display cost-related information.

explanation.summary: The AWS Service Health Dashboard shows service availability.
explanation.additionalInfo: The AWS Service Health Dashboard provides a real-time view of the operational status of AWS services. It is commonly referenced in exam questions related to service availability and incident response.

explanation.summary: There is no general AWS Security Dashboard page.
explanation.why: Security information is accessed through services like Security Hub, not a public status URL.

questions.question: Which of the following procedures can reduce latency when your end users are retrieving data? (Choose TWO)

options.text: Store media assets in the region closest to your end users.

explanation.summary: Placing data closer to users reduces network latency.
examples: Hosting content in a nearby AWS region
explanation.additionalInfo: Latency is highly affected by physical distance. Storing data in regions closest to users is a foundational performance optimization strategy in AWS architectures.

options.text: Store media assets on an additional EBS volume and increase the capacity of your server.

explanation.summary: Increasing storage capacity does not reduce network latency.
explanation.why: Latency is affected by network distance, not local storage size.

options.text: Replicate media assets to at least two availability zones.

explanation.summary: Multi-AZ replication improves availability, not latency.
explanation.why: Replication across AZs does not reduce the distance to end users.

options.text: Reduce the size of media assets using the Amazon Elastic Transcoder.

explanation.summary: Smaller files can help throughput but are not the best latency-focused answer here.
explanation.why: While file size affects transfer time, the primary latency reduction strategies tested are proximity and CDN usage.

options.text: Store media assets in $3 and use CloudFront to distribute these assets.

explanation.summary: Using CloudFront delivers content from edge locations.
explanation.additionalInfo: Amazon CloudFront caches content at edge locations worldwide, reducing the distance between users and data. This is one of the most common AWS exam answers for latency reduction.

questions.question: Which of the following are part of the seven design principles for security in the cloud? (Choose TWO)

options.text: Use manual monitoring techniques to protect your AWS resources.

explanation.summary: Manual monitoring is not a cloud security best practice.
explanation.why: AWS security principles emphasize automation and continuous monitoring, not manual processes.

options.text: Use IAM roles to grant temporary access instead of long-term credentials.

explanation.summary: Temporary credentials reduce risk and improve security.
examples: Using IAM roles for EC2 instances
explanation.additionalInfo: Using IAM roles with temporary credentials is a fundamental AWS security design principle. It minimizes the risk of credential leakage and is strongly emphasized in AWS exams.

options.text: Scale horizontally to protect from failures.

explanation.summary: Horizontal scaling is a reliability principle.
explanation.why: While important, horizontal scaling is not one of the security design principles.

explanation.summary: Real-time traceability improves detection and response.
explanation.additionalInfo: Real-time traceability ensures that actions can be monitored, logged, and audited continuously. AWS emphasizes this principle to improve security visibility and rapid incident response.

options.text: Never store sensitive data in the cloud.

explanation.summary: AWS supports storing sensitive data securely.
explanation.why: AWS provides encryption and compliance capabilities that allow secure storage of sensitive data.

questions.question: A company is migrating production workloads to AWS, and they are concerned about cost management across different departments. Which option should the company implement to categorize and track AWS spending?

options.text: Use the AWS Pricing Calculator service to monitor the costs incurred by each department.

explanation.summary: Pricing Calculator estimates costs, not track them.
explanation.why: The Pricing Calculator is used for forecasting, not tracking real usage by department.

options.text: Use Amazon Aurora to forecast AWS spending based on usage.

explanation.summary: Aurora is a database service.
explanation.why: Aurora does not provide cost tracking or forecasting capabilities.

options.text: Apply cost allocation tags to segment AWS costs by different e projects and departments.

explanation.summary: Cost allocation tags enable detailed cost tracking.
keyPoints: Tag resources by department or project
explanation.additionalInfo: Cost allocation tags allow organizations to categorize AWS usage and costs. They integrate with Cost Explorer and Cost & Usage Reports, making them essential for departmental cost management.

options.text: Configure AWS Price List API to receive billing updates for each department automatically.

explanation.summary: Price List API provides pricing information.
explanation.why: It does not track actual usage or allocate costs by department.

questions.question: What is the main benefit of attaching security groups to an Amazon RDS instance?

options.text: Manages user access and encryption keys.

explanation.summary: Security groups do not manage users or encryption keys.
explanation.why: IAM and KMS handle identity and encryption, not security groups.

options.text: Controls what IP address ranges can connect to your database instance.

explanation.summary: Security groups act as network firewalls for RDS.
examples: Allowing access only from application servers
explanation.additionalInfo: Security groups attached to Amazon RDS instances control inbound network traffic. They restrict which IP addresses or security groups can connect, making them essential for database security.

options.text: Deploys SSL/TLS certificates for use with your database instance.

explanation.summary: Certificates are managed separately.
explanation.why: SSL/TLS certificates are configured through database and AWS services, not security groups.

options.text: Distributes incoming traffic across multiple targets.

explanation.summary: Traffic distribution is handled by load balancers.
explanation.why: Security groups do not balance traffic.

questions.question: A company wants to use Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) to run its containerized applications. For compliance reasons, the company wants to retain complete visibility and control over the underlying server cluster. Which Amazon ECS launch type will satisfy these requirements?

explanation.summary: The EC2 launch type provides full control over the underlying instances.
keyPoints: Full visibility into OS and infrastructure
explanation.additionalInfo: With the EC2 launch type, customers manage the EC2 instances that form the ECS cluster. This provides full visibility and control, which is required for certain compliance and regulatory use cases.

explanation.summary: Fargate abstracts server management.
explanation.why: Fargate does not provide visibility or control over the underlying servers.

explanation.summary: Lightsail is not an ECS launch type.
explanation.why: Amazon Lightsail is a separate service and does not apply to ECS.

explanation.summary: Lambda is a serverless compute service.
explanation.why: Lambda is not an ECS launch type and does not provide server control.

questions.question: You have multiple standalone AWS accounts and you want to decrease your AWS monthly charges. What should you do?

options.text: Try to remove unnecessary AWS accounts.

explanation.summary: Removing accounts does not reduce usage costs.
explanation.why: Costs are driven by resource usage, not the number of accounts.

options.text: Add the accounts to an AWS Organization and use Consolidated Billing.

explanation.summary: Consolidated billing combines usage for discounts.
examples: Combining EC2 usage for lower pricing
explanation.additionalInfo: Using AWS Organizations with consolidated billing allows customers to combine usage across multiple accounts, which can reduce costs by qualifying for volume-based pricing discounts.

options.text: Track the AWS charges that are incurred by the member accounts.

explanation.summary: Tracking costs does not reduce them.
explanation.why: Monitoring helps visibility but does not directly decrease charges.

options.text: Enable AWS tiered-pricing before provisioning resources.

explanation.summary: Tiered pricing is automatic.
explanation.why: AWS pricing tiers are applied automatically and cannot be manually enabled.

questions.question: You have been tasked with auditing the security of your VPC. As part of this process, you need to start by analyzing what inbound and outbound traffic is allowed on your EC2 instances. What two parts of the VPC do you need to check to accomplish this task?

explanation.summary: Traffic Manager is not a VPC security component.
explanation.why: Traffic Manager is unrelated to AWS VPC traffic controls.

explanation.summary: Subnets do not directly control traffic rules.
explanation.why: Traffic rules are enforced by Network ACLs and Security Groups, not subnets alone.

explanation.summary: Internet Gateways provide connectivity, not traffic filtering.
explanation.why: IGWs enable internet access but do not define allowed traffic rules.

explanation.summary: Security Groups and Network ACLs define allowed traffic.
explanation.additionalInfo: To audit allowed inbound and outbound traffic in a VPC, both Security Groups and Network ACLs must be reviewed. Together, they provide layered network security controls in AWS.

questions.question: What does the AWS 'Business' support plan provide? (Choose TWO)

options.text: Access to the full set of Trusted Advisor checks.

explanation.summary: Business Support includes the complete Trusted Advisor checks.
explanation.additionalInfo: AWS Business Support provides access to the full set of Trusted Advisor checks. This is a key differentiator between Business and lower-tier support plans and is frequently tested in exams.

explanation.summary: Support Concierge is part of Enterprise Support.
explanation.why: The Support Concierge Service is not included in the Business support plan.

options.text: Less than 15 minutes response-time support if your business critical system goes down.

explanation.summary: 15-minute response times are for Enterprise Support.
explanation.why: Business Support has longer response times for critical issues compared to Enterprise.

explanation.summary: Business Support includes access to the AWS Support API.
explanation.additionalInfo: The AWS Support API is available with Business and Enterprise support plans, enabling programmatic interaction with AWS Support. This capability is commonly tested in AWS exam questions.

explanation.summary: Proactive TAM is exclusive to Enterprise Support.
explanation.why: Business Support does not include a dedicated Technical Account Manager.

questions.question: You have just finished writing your application code. Which service can be used to automate the deployment and scaling of your application?

explanation.summary: Amazon S3 provides object storage.
explanation.why: S3 stores data but does not deploy or scale applications.

explanation.summary: Elastic Beanstalk automates application deployment and scaling.
explanation.additionalInfo: AWS Elastic Beanstalk allows developers to deploy applications without managing the underlying infrastructure. It automatically handles scaling, monitoring, and updates, making it a standard exam choice for simplified deployment scenarios.

explanation.summary: CodeCommit stores source code.
explanation.why: CodeCommit does not handle deployment or scaling.

explanation.summary: EFS provides shared file storage.
explanation.why: EFS does not automate application deployment or scaling.

questions.question: Which statement is true in relation to security in AWS?

options.text: AWS manages everything related to EC2 operating systems.

explanation.summary: Customers manage EC2 operating systems.
explanation.why: Under the shared responsibility model, customers are responsible for the OS on EC2.

options.text: AWS customers are responsible for patching any database software running on Amazon EC2.

explanation.summary: Customers manage software on EC2 instances.
keyPoints: Part of security in the cloud
explanation.additionalInfo: When databases are deployed on Amazon EC2, customers are responsible for managing and patching the database software. This distinction between EC2 and managed services like RDS is a common exam topic.

options.text: Server side encryption is the responsibility of AWS.

explanation.summary: Encryption configuration is shared.
explanation.why: Customers choose and configure encryption settings for their data.

options.text: AWS is responsible for the security of your application.

explanation.summary: Application security is a customer responsibility.
explanation.why: Customers are responsible for securing their applications and data.

questions.question: Amazon EC2 instances are conceptually very similar to traditional servers. However, using Amazon EC2 server instances in the same manner as traditional hardware server instances is only a starting point. What are the main benefits of using the AWS EC2 instances instead of traditional servers? (Choose TWO)

explanation.summary: EC2 supports architectures that improve fault tolerance compared to traditional servers.
explanation.additionalInfo: EC2 instances can be launched, replaced, and distributed across Availability Zones, enabling fault-tolerant architectures that are difficult to achieve with traditional on-premises servers.

options.text: Provides your business with a seamless remote accessibility.

explanation.summary: Remote access is not unique to EC2.
explanation.why: Traditional servers can also be accessed remotely and this is not a defining EC2 advantage.

options.text: Prevents unauthorized users from getting into your network.

explanation.summary: Network security requires proper configuration.
explanation.why: EC2 provides tools like security groups, but prevention depends on customer configuration.

explanation.summary: Backups are not automatic by default.
explanation.why: EC2 requires customers to configure backups using services like EBS snapshots.

options.text: Can be scaled manually in a shorter period of time.

explanation.summary: EC2 enables rapid scaling compared to physical servers.
examples: Launching new instances during traffic spikes
explanation.additionalInfo: EC2 allows customers to provision or terminate compute capacity within minutes. This agility is a major advantage over traditional hardware-based servers and is frequently emphasized in AWS exams.

questions.question: Which statement is true regarding AWS pricing? (Choose TWO)

options.text: With the AWS pay-as-you-go pricing model, you don't have to pay any upfront fee.

explanation.summary: AWS pay-as-you-go pricing has no upfront commitment.
keyPoints: Pay only for what you use
explanation.additionalInfo: AWS pay-as-you-go pricing allows customers to consume services without upfront payments or long-term contracts. This flexibility is a fundamental AWS pricing concept tested in exams.

options.text: You have no responsibility for third-party software license costs.

explanation.summary: Customers may still be responsible for licenses.
explanation.why: Some third-party software requires separate licensing costs.

options.text: You only pay for the individual services that you need with no long-term contracts.

explanation.summary: AWS allows service-by-service billing without contracts.
explanation.additionalInfo: AWS pricing is service-based, allowing customers to pay only for the services they use. There are no required long-term commitments, reinforcing the flexibility of the cloud pricing model.

options.text: For some services, you have to pay a startup fee in order to get the service running.

explanation.summary: AWS generally does not charge startup fees.
explanation.why: Most AWS services can be started without any setup fees.

options.text: There are no reservations on AWS, you only pay for what you use.

explanation.summary: AWS offers reservation options.
explanation.why: Reserved Instances and Savings Plans exist for discounted pricing.

questions.question: Which AWS service provides the EASIEST way to set up and manage a secure, well-architected, multi-account AWS environment?

explanation.summary: AWS Control Tower simplifies multi-account governance.
explanation.additionalInfo: AWS Control Tower provides the easiest and fastest way to set up a secure, multi-account AWS environment following best practices. It automates account creation, governance, and guardrail enforcement.

explanation.summary: Amazon Macie focuses on data security.
explanation.why: Macie detects sensitive data but does not manage multi-account environments.

explanation.summary: Patch Manager automates patching.
explanation.why: It does not set up or govern multi-account environments.

options.text: AWS Systems Manager Patch Manager AWS Security Hub.

explanation.summary: This is not a valid AWS service option.
explanation.why: It incorrectly combines two separate services.
